label: 0056 · Smoothed in time, 1997–2025 (one QP over 53 windows): 0054 with the BEL following the slab through the cold nose (the interface down to 70 km, then a curtain up to the 30 km sheet), uncorrelated noise, background coupling from −1 to 1, fourteen slow slip events as signal, fixed 747-site network, UNR positions (MAP)
description: 0054 on a base whose BEL follows the slab beneath the coast, as the cold nose of the mantle-wedge corner would make it (Sun et al., 2014; Freed et al., 2017; Luo and Wang, 2021). The sheet runs along the slab interface from the trench mesh's 50 km bottom edge down to 70 km (extrapolated with the dip of its deepest triangles), then up a vertical curtain beneath the 70 km line to the 30 km sheet landward of it. Offshore it is 0054. Beneath the coast, flow in the hot wedge acts on the curtain and on the interface at 50–70 km. That part of the BEL slips 226 mm in the first year after Tohoku and 401 mm in 2012–2021. Megathrust coupling at 20–50 km off Miyagi averages about −2.5 in 2012–2021 (0053: −0.9 to −1.4). Seafloor cross-validation is +1,044 and onshore window cross-validation +465, against +1,138 and +548 for 0054. It does better before Tohoku (+93 against +20) and worse in the first week after it, so there is no overall gain. Seafloor data: Japan Coast Guard (CC BY-NC 4.0) and Tohoku University (CC BY 4.0).
